en.title: Stress Is Not Written
en.summary: Romanian letters do not mark stress, so you must use audio and dictionaries to find the strong syllable.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: In every word, one syllable is stronger. You give it more power. You say it slightly louder and longer. Listen to (limbă) /ˈlim.bə/, which means language. The first part is strong. The voice falls on the second part. Stress gives the word its natural rhythm.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Open your mouth a little wider on the stressed syllable. Push more air from your lungs. Do not change the vowel sound. Keep every vowel clean and clear. For (copil) /koˈpil/, which means child, push air on the second syllable. Your tone rises slightly on the strong part, then drops softly.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Standard letters never show where the stress goes. You cannot see a stress mark in normal texts. Because of this, you must listen carefully. You can also check a good dictionary. Dictionaries mark the strong vowel for you. Always learn a new word together with its sound.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not guess the stress pattern. Many learners stress the wrong syllable. If you say (limbă) /ˈlim.bə/ with stress at the end, it sounds wrong. Do not look for written accent marks on the page. Instead, rely on audio recordings. Train your ears to catch the beat every time.
